A Space’s Corner

Where will people build the first permanent bases on the Moon and Mars? A Space’s Corner shows the most likely base sites and the places on Earth that resemble them: deserts, volcanoes, caves, ice and salt flats where scientists test ideas and equipment. Explore them on 3D globes and maps, and read about each place in the dictionary.

      • Initial observations from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA)Smith et al., 2010, Geophysical Research Letters 37:L18204LOLA instrument and first lunar topography results
      • Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter: Experiment summary after the first year of global mapping of MarsSmith et al., 2001, Journal of Geophysical Research 106:23689–23722MOLA global topography of Mars
      • Mars Viking Global Color Mosaic 925mUSGS Astrogeology Science Center, n.d.Viking Orbiter colour mosaic used for the Mars globe texture
      • Three.jsthree.js authors, n.d.JavaScript 3D library used to render the globes

      Papers are linked through their DOI. The notes on the Moon and Mars sites draw on each site’s Wikipedia article, checked against the papers and agency pages listed with it. Figures on this site are rounded; coordinates are approximate.

      FAQ

      Frequently asked questions

      What is A Space’s Corner?

      A bilingual field guide to the places most likely to host the first permanent bases on the Moon and Mars, and to the places on Earth that resemble them.

      What is an Earth analog?

      A place on Earth whose rocks, landforms or conditions are similar to a site on the Moon or Mars. Scientists use analogs to test rovers, spacesuits, instruments and mission plans, and to train astronauts, before going to space.

      What do the marker colours mean?

      Blue is a Moon site or Moon analog, red is a Mars site or Mars analog, and half blue, half red is an Earth analog for both. A marker with a white part is a proposed analog that has potential but has not been field-tested yet: colour on top and white below for one world, or blue, red and white thirds for both.

      How do I find a place?

      Type its name in the search box of the Map explorer and pick a result, or browse the Dictionary. The Dictionary can be filtered by Earth, Moon or Mars and sorted from A to Z, by continent or by country.

      What is the difference between the card and Details?

      Clicking a marker opens a short card with the basics. Press Details to see the place’s photos, its fun fact and more to know.

      What are the Terrain, Atmospheric pressure and Average temperature views?

      They are extra map layers for Earth. Terrain colours the land and the seafloor by height, Atmospheric pressure shows the average air pressure at the ground, and Average temperature shows the average air temperature near the ground, both for 1991–2020. Click any spot on these layers to pin a reading.

      What are the Mars Terrain, Atmospheric pressure and Radiation views?

      They are map layers for Mars, worked out from the ground height measured by the MOLA laser altimeter. Terrain colours the ground by its height; Mars has no sea, so heights are measured from an agreed reference level (the datum). Atmospheric pressure is an annual-mean estimate: the air on Mars is so thin that it presses with less than 1% of Earth’s sea-level pressure, most in the deep Hellas basin and least on top of the giant volcanoes. Radiation is the estimated daily dose from cosmic rays at the surface, in millisieverts (mSv), scaled from the Curiosity rover’s measurement at Gale Crater: the more air overhead, the lower the dose. Point at any spot to read its value, or click it to pin the reading.

      Where does the information come from?

      From scientific papers, space agencies, geological surveys and reliable news reports. Every source is listed on the Sources page. Figures are rounded and coordinates are approximate.

      How do I change the language or switch to dark mode?

      Open Settings with the gear button at the bottom of the taskbar, then choose English or Tiếng Việt and Light or Dark.

      How can I see the tutorial again?

      Press the button below. In the tutorial you can also choose whether it shows each time you open the website.

      About us

      A Space’s Corner

      A field guide that identifies Earth locations analogous to the likely permanent base sites on the Moon and Mars.

      Our goal: Linking Earth science and space exploration by mapping land environments that mirror unearthly conditions to support future Moon and Mars missions.
